SOL02-D11.rationale: With has_previous=false there is no previous bidder whose live bid record is meaningful; differences in the passed-in prev_bid_of echo are a don't-care artifact of the abstraction. pending remains meaningful on every input.

SOL03-D08.rationale: owed is the amount still owed when the reward transfer fails, so it is meaningful failure-path state rather than a sentinel payload.

TS03-D09.rationale: The benchmark models Math.round with integer division. Truncation and nearest-integer rounding differ by at most one cent in the discounted amount, so exact equality would overblock the source-like rounding implementation; differences larger than one cent remain blocking evidence.

TS03-D03.rationale: The canonical model intentionally fixes multiplication-before-division integer arithmetic. Reordering division before multiplication loses precision in the chosen integer model and is meaningful divergence, not a rounding abstraction boundary.

GO01-D04.rationale: The no-SKU branch is the adjudicated error/default boundary and the SKU-present branch is the success boundary. Both inputs satisfy len(parts) == n && n >= 3, and the success input has four columns so the buggy indexed reference is defined there. For the buggy reference this error input is an adjudicated out-of-bounds domain error; a verifiably defined candidate on that input is diagnostic behavioral divergence. Finite agreement is diagnostic evidence only.

PY02-D04.rationale: A row shorter than four columns is the adjudicated error boundary, while a four-column row exercises successful indexed access. Both inputs satisfy len(row) == n. For the buggy reference this error input is an adjudicated out-of-bounds domain error; a verifiably defined candidate on that input is diagnostic behavioral divergence. Finite agreement is diagnostic evidence only.

SOL01-D03.rationale: Zero shares exercises the adjudicated default/error branch and positive shares exercises successful division without overflowing the integer model. For the buggy reference the zero-share input is an adjudicated division-by-zero domain error; a verifiably defined candidate on that input is diagnostic behavioral divergence. Finite agreement is diagnostic evidence only.

GO02-D03.rationale: A negative top is the adjudicated rejection/error boundary, while a positive in-range top exercises the success boundary. Both inputs satisfy n_paths >= 0. For the buggy reference the negative input is an adjudicated slice/system-boundary domain error because paths[:end] is invalid; a verifiably defined candidate on that input is diagnostic behavioral divergence. Finite agreement is diagnostic evidence only.

PY02-D05.rationale: The overtime loop is stateful across array indices. The concrete inputs cover the recorded first-day counterexample, a case where only a later day contributes, exact threshold boundaries, and a three-day mixed aggregation; agreement on these inputs is finite diagnostic evidence only.
